name: Note Highway
description: The scrolling lanes: chart data becomes notes that travel toward a receptor line at a readable approach rate. It owns lane geometry, spawn/despawn bookkeeping, and the approach seconds that convert song time into screen space — the one translation no other component is positioned to do. It deliberately owns no timing truth of its own: every position derives from utility.beat_clock's song position, so pausing, seeking, or latency recalibration moves the whole highway consistently instead of desyncing lanes from audio. It also does not judge — a note crossing the receptor is announced as ui.note_passed_receptor, and utility.judgement_window decides what the crossing meant. Chart parsing is persistence.chart_loader's job; this component consumes loaded chart data, never raw files, so a malformed beatmap fails at load time rather than mid-song.

inputs.name: laneCount
inputs.description: Number of lanes, matched to the chart's note data. Four keys and seven keys are different skills; the highway serves both by not baking the count into its geometry.

inputs.name: approachSeconds
inputs.description: How long a note is visible before reaching the receptor — the difficulty-independent speed setting. Players tune this to taste; judgement windows stay in time, not pixels, so it changes readability, not difficulty.

inputs.name: scrollDirection
inputs.description: down, up, left, or right. Direction is pure presentation — time-to-receptor math is identical — which is why it is one field and not four components.

inputs.name: despawnAfterReceptorSeconds
inputs.description: How long a missed note lingers past the receptor before despawning. Long enough that the miss reads as a miss, not a vanishing.

outputs.name: highwayProgress
outputs.description: 0..1 through the chart, for progress bars and practice-mode seeking.
